stem: A staff nurse is asked to participate in a unit quality-improvement project addressing repeated delays in pain reassessment. Which response is most appropriate?

options.A: Participate in the project and contribute relevant client-care observations and data
options.B: Decline because quality-improvement activities are outside the role of a staff RN
options.C: Wait for an executive administrator to identify every client-care issue before participating
options.D: Avoid reporting care-process problems unless a client files a formal complaint

rationale: The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan includes participation in performance-improvement projects and quality-improvement processes, reporting identified client-care issues to appropriate personnel, and using research and references for performance-improvement actions. A staff RN can appropriately contribute observations and data to a unit quality-improvement effort. The other responses incorrectly exclude the RN from quality improvement or delay identification of care problems.
educational_objective: Recognize participation in unit quality-improvement processes and reporting of client-care issues as appropriate responsibilities of the RN.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

correction_summary: Reframed the source item's shared-governance council terminology into an entry-level RN quality-improvement participation item. This preserves the staff-engagement concept while mapping directly to NCSBN 2026 activity statements rather than relying on a specific organizational governance model.
